{{Quote|What's the last thing to go through an Imperial scout trooper's head when he hits a tree? His afterburner.|Joke told by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] forces on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]|<ref name="Vehs&Vessels" />}}
The '''74-Z speeder bike''', sometimes referred to as the '''Imperial speeder bike''' due to its use by [[Scout trooper/Legends|scout]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], was a [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]] manufactured by [[Aratech Repulsor Company/Legends|Aratech Repulsor Company]] used for reconnaissance purposes, as well as rapid transportation in combat zones.

==Characteristics==
[[File:74Zspeederbike_schem.jpg|thumb|left|250px|74-Z [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]].]]
They were capable of reaching speeds up to and beyond five hundred kilometers per hour, and had a flight ceiling of twenty-five meters. 74-Zs were the military variant of the civilian [[74-Y speeder bike|74-Y]]. They were controlled by handlebars located towards the front of the vehicle, and foot pedals slung underneath adjusted speed and altitude.

The highly maneuverable vehicles were equipped with [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] and communications devices located between the handlebars, including a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] and a [[Jammer/Legends|comlink-jamming device]]. The speeder was equipped with terrain-following sensors that linked up with the HUD in the driver's helmet.<ref name="Handbook" /> They were armed with a forward rotating [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannon]] for combat.

They were also equipped with a very powerful boost that could propel them over vast distances in a shorter amount of time.<ref name="RS III">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref> In addition, the 74-Z was stripped down to just its fundamental components, namely the engine and steering vane, in order to increase its overall speed, and as such a single, scaled-down, forward-facing blaster cannon was fixed on the undercarriage. Rebel ace pilot [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] admitted that he was uncomfortable piloting them due to being essentially an engine and a steering vane.<ref name="Handbook" />

==History==
[[File:74ZMilitarySpeederBike-SW2Indy.png|thumb|left|250px|A scout trooper riding a 74-Z speeder bike]]
Used by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] along with the younger [[BARC speeder/Legends|BARC speeders]], these speeder bikes saw action on many worlds. The bike was first used during the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]]. The 74-Z was capable of being deployed from [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|LAAT/i]] [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]]. On the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Stass Allie/Legends|Stass Allie]] was [[Order 66/Legends|killed by her own troops]] while riding a 74-Z bike. It was also used by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="Jedi Trial" />

[[File:PaplooJacksARide-ROTJ.png|thumb|right|300px|The Ewok [[Paploo/Legends|Paploo]] steals a 74-Z]]
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], both the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] utilized these speeder bikes, though Aratech primarily supplied the vehicles to Imperial forces. On the forest moon of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], Imperial scout troopers engaged in a vicious chase with [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] after the Rebels commandeered speeder bikes to pursue their foes. 74-Zs subsequently saw use in the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|battle]] that followed.<ref name="SWE6" />

74-Zs were later used in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]] on [[Myrkr system|Myrkr]] while [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] [[Rescue on Myrkr|obtained supplies]] for his campaign.<ref name="Heir to the Empire">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The speeder bikes appear in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars:'' Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], and were based on concept art by [[Joe Johnston]] and [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]].

[[Hasbro]] later took a piece of the concept art and created the [[Star Wars Legends|expanded universe]] vehicle the [[Aratech Military Speeder Bike Prototype]] for their [[Star Wars: The Power of the Force (1995 toy line)|''Star Wars: The Power of the Force'']] toyline.<ref name="Hasbro">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: The Power of the Force (1995 toy line)|pack=Speeder Bike|link=potf2euspeederbike.asp}}</ref>

These speeder bikes were meant to be shown during the Battle of [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']], but their scenes were cut at the animatics stage. Despite this, one was featured in a 2003, the 4482 LEGO AT-TE set as part of the [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] line and another in the 2008, the 7676 LEGO Republic Gunship set as part of the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'']] line.

''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' erroneously states the 74-Z is three meters long.

In the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]'', a 74-Z is visible in one of ''[[Prosecutor]]''{{'s}} Docking Bays. It was referred to as "a death trap" by [[Scorch/Legends|Scorch]]. It could be used to destroy the B1 battle droid dispenser without having to use a demo charge on it by hacking the terminal next to the 74-Z to launch it into the dispenser.
